name: Representation-Sensitive Recognition and Completion for Learning Spaces
statement: For an explicit medium with $n$ states, $m$ transitions, and $\tau$ token pairs, a given orientation can be tested for closedness in $O(m\log n)$ time with a violating state and token pair, and a closed orientation can be found or ruled out in $O(m\tau)$ time. For a listed candidate base $\mathcal B$, with $b=|\mathcal B|$ and total member size $s$, one can decide in $O(bs)$ time whether it is the base of a learning space: exactly when $\varnothing\in\mathcal B$ and every nonempty member has exactly one endpoint. A minimal well-graded extension of an arbitrary listed family is constructible in polynomial time, while deciding whether all listed input members can remain base members of some learning space is NP-complete.
proof: These are the cited medium-orientation, base-recognition, and extension theorems. Trying each of the $n$ states as a root and testing the induced orientation yields the derived $O(nm\log n)$ recognition bound for learning-space graphs represented as explicit finite media. Minimal extension means inclusion-minimal, not minimum cardinality.
